cases.reply: A virtual key is the secret an app sends to LiteLLM Proxy to authenticate requests. A team groups people and their keys under shared budgets and model permissions. Use separate keys for your apps, and put them in a team when a project or department needs shared ownership and limits.

Virtual keys authenticate callers; teams manage members and keys together. Give an integration its own key for proxy API calls. If several apps and people share a project budget or model access rules, group their keys in a team; an isolated integration can use a standalone key.
Keys are for apps; teams are for organization. Use keys for individual needs and teams for shared needs. You can use both.
A virtual key is a label for an application, while a team ID is the credential you send to LiteLLM Proxy. Use the team ID for API requests and virtual keys to organize members and shared budgets.

A virtual key is the credential an app sends to LiteLLM Proxy. Teams group members and keys under shared budgets and model access. Every key must belong to a team, so create a team even for a single isolated integration before issuing its key.
